name: Harry Marillier
bio: Henry Currie Marillier, a Bluecoat Boy (pupil of Christ's Hospital, then still in London) 1875-84, lodged at 13 Salisbury Street, Strand, while Wilde was living there in 1880-81 and, as a boy, brought Wilde his coffee. Classical scholar of Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1884-87; his autumn-1885 letter to Wilde, inviting him to the Cambridge Eumenides, opened the 1885-86 correspondence. He later became an engineer and partner in W. A. S. Benson's metalworks, then a literary and art journalist, editing The Early Work of Aubrey Beardsley (1899) and writing on tapestry.
bio_note: All facts from the main-particulars footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 266 n. 3, plus the coffee/Salisbury Street recollection in Wilde's letter of [Postmark 5 November 1885] at the same page.
